items.back: Raja Ram Mohan Roy (1828); campaign led to Sati ban (Regulation XVII, 1829). 'Father of Indian Renaissance'.
items.examPoint: Raja Ram Mohan Roy & Brahmo Samaj (1828); abolition of Sati (Regulation XVII, 1829)

items.back: Brahmo Samaj of India (1866), Indian Reform Association (1870), Church of the New Dispensation/Nava Vidhan (1880).
items.examPoint: Dalit journalism (Gopal Baba Walangkar, Vital-Vidhvansak 1888) & Keshab Chandra Sen (Indian Reform Association, New Dispensation)

items.back: Dayananda Saraswati (1875); 'Back to the Vedas'; Shuddhi movement; Satyarth Prakash.
items.examPoint: Dayananda Saraswati, Arya Samaj (1875) & Shuddhi / back-to-the-Vedas

items.back: Swami Vivekananda (1897); addressed the World Parliament of Religions, Chicago, 1893.
items.examPoint: Ramakrishna, Vivekananda & Ramakrishna Mission (1897); Parliament of Religions (1893)

items.back: 1867, Bombay; M.G. Ranade (also Atmaram Pandurang). Caste equality, widow remarriage.
Jyotirao Phule (1873, Maharashtra); anti-caste movement; wrote Gulamgiri.

items.front: Widow remarriage & age of consent — laws & reformers?
items.back: Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act 1856 (Vidyasagar); Age of Consent Act 1891 (Behramji Malabari).
items.examPoint: Women's reform & legislation (Age of Consent Act 1891, Savitribai Phule, Pandita Ramabai, Annie Besant)

items.back: Gopal Baba Walangkar (1888); first monthly for the Depressed Classes. (Ambedkar is a distractor.)
items.examPoint: Dalit journalism (Gopal Baba Walangkar, Vital-Vidhvansak 1888) & Keshab Chandra Sen (Indian Reform Association, New Dispensation)

items.back: Restitution of conjugal rights, age of consent, women's education; fed the Age of Consent Act 1891.
items.examPoint: Women's reform cases & schools — Rakhmabai case (1884), Bethune School (Vidyasagar)

items.back: Founded by J.E.D. Bethune (Calcutta, 1849); Vidyasagar was its secretary; female education.
items.examPoint: Women's reform cases & schools — Rakhmabai case (1884), Bethune School (Vidyasagar)

items.front: Reform-text chronology: Neel Darpan, Arya Samaj, Anandamath?
items.back: Neel Darpan 1860 → Arya Samaj 1875 → Anandamath 1882 (Vande Mataram).
items.examPoint: Reform-text chronology (Neel Darpan 1860, Arya Samaj 1875, Anandamath 1882) & Theosophical Society (Blavatsky/Olcott 1875, Adyar 1882, Besant)

items.front: Theosophical Society — founders, HQ, later leader?
items.back: Blavatsky & Olcott (New York 1875); HQ Adyar, Madras (1882); later Annie Besant.
items.examPoint: Reform-text chronology (Neel Darpan 1860, Arya Samaj 1875, Anandamath 1882) & Theosophical Society (Blavatsky/Olcott 1875, Adyar 1882, Besant)

items.back: Periyar E.V. Ramaswami (Tamil Nadu, 1925, rationalist, Kudi Arasu); Sree Narayana Guru: SNDP/Aravippuram, 'One caste, one religion, one God'.
items.examPoint: Caste & self-respect movements (Periyar Self-Respect, Justice Party 1916, Aravippuram 1888)

items.front: Father of Telugu Renaissance & first Telugu widow remarriage?
items.back: Kandukuri Veeresalingam; first widow remarriage at Rajahmundry (1881); journal Vivekavardhini.
items.examPoint: Kandukuri Veeresalingam — Telugu social reform, first widow remarriage (1881), Vivekavardhini

items.back: Gurajada wrote Kanyasulkam (1892) against bride-price; Gidugu led the Vyavaharika Bhasha (spoken Telugu) movement; 29 Aug = Telugu Language Day.
